messages:
sophia: quick sync on attribute tiering for observability ingest. we need a concrete, implementable plan for what to keep hot vs defer for cost attribution and investigations.
liam: can you summarize the realistic tradeoffs again? cost to ingest/index vs query latency/complexity? :thinking_face:
maya: short: more attrs = higher ingest and index cardinality. that hits storage and query cost. but less attrs means painful forensic queries and billing lookups.
sophia: sketched options: full-retain (everything stays), compact-default (only billing keys + small set), or minimal-with-late-enrich (minimal keys only, rest in enrichment store joined at query time).
liam: late-enrich lowers steady ingest costs but makes common dashboards slower if they need joins. sampled traces make joins hairy if attr snapshots are lost.
infra-bot: RFC: https://redwood.local/rfcs/2025-obsv-attr-contract (see appendix with example schemas)
maya: proposal: define attribute tiers: tier0 (must keep: tenant_id, org_id, env, billing_id), tier1 (service/route/error_class/instance), tier2 (user metadata, custom tags). keep tier0 always hot, tier1 configurable per-service, tier2 deferred to enrichment.
sophia: agree. default policy: compact with per-service overrides. concrete policy example: 
```yaml
service_obsv_policy:
  default: compact
  overrides:
    auth-service: full
  tiers:
    tier0: [tenant_id, org_id, env, billing_id]
    tier1: [service, route, error_class, instance]
    tier2: [user_tags, sdk_meta, custom_tags]
```
liam: need per-tenant overrides too. large enterprise customers will require tier1 hot. also, we must document transform rules (hashing/truncation) for each key under compact to avoid disputes.
maya: enrichment design: append-only attr blobs stored cold, keyed by attr_blob_id. ingest writes attr_blob_id into compact envelope. query side joins on attr_blob_id with LRU caching for recent blobs. enrichment blobs are immutable for a short retention window.
sophia: sampling interaction: if trace carries sample header (x-trace-sample=1) the agent should snapshot tier1 into the trace even if policy is compact. preserves fidelity for sampled SLO/forensics.
liam: migration/rollout: keep previous full attrs in cold store for 90 days for reconciliation/backfill. canary: roll compact default on 5% of services for 14 days, monitor query latencies and % of late-enrich hits.
maya: metrics to watch: ingest bytes per-minute per-service, 95p query latency for cost dashboards, rate of failed joins (attr_blob missing). set alert if join-failure > 0.1% or 95p latency regresses > 20%.
sophia: action items: liam -> draft canonical tier key list and transform table (hash/trim rules). maya -> prototype attr-blob format, storage layout, and cache TTL. sophia -> implement ingest flag, feature flag for per-service policy, and canary dashboard.
deploy-bot: feature flag created: feature.obs.attr_tiering (scoped: org:infra).
infra-bot: ticket RW-OBS-712 created: obs-attr-tiering-rollout.
liam: final Q: how reversible are transforms? we must keep pointer to raw blob for billing disputes; transforms should be documented but preserve a reversible reference.
maya: we'll include reversible pointer (attr_blob_id) to raw payload and document non-reversible ops (e.g., irreversible redaction) per-tenant policy.
sophia: good. i'll update the RFC with tier list, transform table, migration appendix, and canary plan. aim to post an RFC revision and PoC next week. :thumbsup:
liam: :thumbsup:
maya: :rocket:
